subject: Capacity allocator: fallback & OEM quote alignment (Vanguard.Health - VHG-349)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: alice@quantacloud.com, ryan@cloudbridge.io
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity allocator: fallback & OEM quote alignment (Vanguard.Health - VHG-349)

Hi Alice + Ryan —

Quick context: Vanguard.Health (deal VHG-349) signaled a firm go-live window for October; they want a dedicated pool profile that ramps over Q4. We need to lock hardware commitment cadence and an interim backfill option while OEM lead times run.

Ask: can QuantaCloud confirm (1) earliest partial shipment cadence you can commit to (e.g., 30% at week N, 40% at week N+4), (2) firm lead-time range per SKU, and (3) whether you can insert a partial-delivery clause in the PO/contract so Vanguard can accept staged units?

Ryan — CloudBridge: can you hold burst capacity for Vanguard as a backstop? If QuantaCloud cannot provide staged deliveries early enough we want to use CloudBridge for the first 8–12 weeks and then transition to QuantaCloud reserved capacity. Please flag pricing for 0–40% burst and minimum hold windows.

Im cc'ing Karthik and Laura to sketch a triage plan (reserved vs hybrid) once we have the OEM ETA. Attached: initial capacity matrix (draft) — well iterate.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_matrix_vhg349.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Alice Romero <alice@quantacloud.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ryan@cloudbridge.io
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity allocator: fallback & OEM quote alignment (Vanguard.Health - VHG-349)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the heads-up. Attached is our formal OEM quote and a proposed tranche schedule. High-level: the SKUs Vanguard requested (QC-A1000-L and QC-A1000-S) are currently at a 14–18 week manufacturing + allocation lead time for first full shipment. We can prioritize a partial build (up to ~35% of the requested capacity) on a separate production lane in ~8–10 weeks, but that requires an explicit partial-shipment clause and a 20% non-refundable deposit on the tranche schedule. Price validity: 30 days from the quote date.

Notes:
- Partial shipments: we can do 35% @ week 9, 40% @ week 15, remainder in week 20 if vendor allocation holds.
- Firmware/config validation: we recommend a pre-shipment validation window (2 weeks) to avoid rework.
- Customs/port variance: add 1–2 weeks expectancy for international shipments.

Ive attached OEM_Quote_QuantaCloud_VHG-349_20250629.pdf and a short terms doc. If Vanguard procurement needs E2E tracking we can add milestone reporting to the SOW.

Best,
Alice Romero
Head of Strategic Accounts, QuantaCloud

Attachments: OEM_Quote_QuantaCloud_VHG-349_20250629.pdf (pdf); production_slot_terms.docx (docx)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: OEM quote + cloud gap plan

Forwarding QuantaCloud's response — please review and propose a concrete fallback.

Action items for internal ops:
- Karthik: run the matrix (attached) and propose two recommended build mixes (committed vs hybrid) with unit economics and SLA delta. We need a fallback that keeps Vanguard within their target latency/cost profile.
- Laura: flag any procurement redlines we should request (partial-shipment acceptance language, deposit terms, warranty start date tied to final acceptance).
- Ben: can we offer a short-term commercial concession (credits or pricing protection) to smooth the staggered delivery effect for the customer?

QuantaCloud suggests 35% partial at ~week9, remainder later. If we can secure CloudBridge for first 8–12 weeks, we can accept staged deliveries and avoid missing the October timeline.

Quoted below:
> On Mon, 30 Jun 2025 at 12:20 PM Alice Romero <alice@quantacloud.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks for the heads-up. Attached is our formal OEM quote and a proposed tranche schedule...

Attachment: capacity_matrix_vhg349.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: OEM quote + cloud gap plan

Jordan —

Reviewed QuantaCloud's tranche schedule and the draft matrix. I ran three baseline options in the attached spreadsheet (we referenced your draft):

Option 1 — Aggressive reserved: 80% QuantaCloud reserved; 20% CloudBridge burst hold. Pros: best unit economics and predictable latency. Cons: exposes us to 14–18 week tail risk if vendor delays.

Option 2 — Hybrid staggered (recommended): 50% QuantaCloud reserved with staged deliveries (35% @ wk9, 15% @ wk15), + 40% CloudBridge burst hold for weeks 0–12, + 10% short-term spot. This keeps Vanguard's service window and keeps cost impact moderate.

Option 3 — Cloud-backstop first: 20% QuantaCloud reserved + 70% CloudBridge burst + 10% spot. Lowest procurement lead risk but highest recurring unit cost and potential performance variance.

Procurement redlines I recommend we push to QuantaCloud: partial-delivery acceptance with pro-rated warranty start (start after final acceptance), milestone-based invoicing tied to shipments, and a firm maximum cumulative lead-time variance (e.g., +2 weeks). If QuantaCloud will not accept those terms we escalate to legal.

Next steps:
- Laura: draft redlines and a short SOW addendum for partial shipments.
- Ben: confirm any commercial concession you can offer to offset Q4 ramp risk for Vanguard (credits or temporary price protection).
- Jordan: if Vanguard accepts Option 2 I will produce a final capacity schedule and update the cost model.

Attachment: capacity_matrix_vhg349.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: OEM quote + cloud gap plan

Short note — agree with Option 2 (hybrid staggered). We can offer Vanguard a 10% consumption credit on CloudBridge burst for the first quarter post-onboard to offset the higher burst cost. That should be enough to keep their TCO within the expected band while the tranche completes.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: alice@quantacloud.com, ryan@cloudbridge.io
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity allocator: fallback & OEM quote alignment (Vanguard.Health - VHG-349)

Alice / Ryan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Internal alignment summary: Redwood is prepared to proceed with Option 2 (Hybrid staggered) for Vanguard (VHG-349):

- Commitment: Redwood will commit to 50% QuantaCloud reserved capacity with QuantaCloud delivering a partial tranche (target 35%) at ~week9 and the remainder per their quoted cadence.
- Backfill: CloudBridge to hold burst capacity up to 40% for weeks 0–12 to cover Vanguards go-live window. Ben has approved a 10% consumption credit for CloudBridge usage in the first quarter post-onboard.
- Contract: Laura will send redlines requesting partial-shipment acceptance, milestone invoicing, and warranty start tied to final acceptance. QuantaCloud: please confirm you will accept staged-delivery language and the proposed tranche cadence. We also need DocuSign for the PO+SOW; ideally a short addendum we can sign this week.

Ryan: please place a soft hold on the 40% burst for VHG-349 and share provisional pricing/DocuSign link for the hold by EOD Thursday.

Alice: please confirm (A) that the 35% partial at week 9 is feasible given your allocation lanes, (B) the earliest date you can commit to shipment milestones in a DocuSign PO, and (C) if you will accept the milestone invoicing approach (deposit on tranche, balance on shipment).

Ill update the HubSpot deal and create an INF Jira ticket for the onboarding checkpoints (link below).

Thanks all — this keeps Vanguard on track for October while hedging lead-time risk.

Jordan Blake
Senior Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
